Code: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh → · ENS: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/blob/main/docs/integrations/ens.md → · The Graph: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/blob/main/docs/integrations/thegraph.md →

🧩 The problem. Memberships live on a plastic card, a dedicated app or a vendor's database, so verification and revocation depend on the issuing system. fuda puts the right on-chain so another verifier can check it. The right should outlive the app.

⛓️ Independently verifiable rights. Each right is an EAS Entitlement on Base Sepolia, issued under an on-chain IssuerDelegation. The hosted gate calls the API, which reads both by eth_call and checks operational state in D1; required chain reads fail closed. Revoke on-chain and the same QR is rejected on the next scan. Anyone can check the on-chain records; reproducing the hosted admission verdict also needs its operational state.
🔐 Standard and +Private. Standard demos use Bearer verification: save a pass, present its QR. Signed adds holder proof through challenge-response, and +Private extends it with a fresh ERC-5564 stealth holder address per issued right, unlocked by a separate fuda PRF passkey prepared before issuance. Real iPhone captures show discovery of rights with distinct stealth holders, ADMIT for an active right and REJECT / REVOKED for a different, previously revoked one. Private issuance currently uses the admin API; its card-claim UI is not connected.
Portable attendance records. Non-private admissions schedule an EAS Attendance attestation asynchronously, best-effort; a failed attestation does not undo admission. +Private emits no public Attendance; entry logs stay in D1.
🏷️ ENS names the relationship; EAS proves the right. ethonline2026.fuda.eth is an entry the venue claimed and owns in an ENSv2 User Registry on Sepolia — non-transferable, expiring, gas sponsored. The member number printed on the pass, <member-no>.ethonline2026.fuda.eth, is a free offchain name answered by a signed CCIP-Read gateway. Both resolve through the hackathon Universal Resolver from a plain viem client, and a manually provisioned +Private member name resolved to two different stealth addresses across two queries. Automated private issuance and naming remain unconnected.
📊 The Graph is on the read path, not beside it. The rights subgraph is what the member app queries for +Private discovery and what the dashboard queries for on-chain status; the API's own announcement cache was deleted when it landed.

The app, dashboard, gate and API are deployed at *.fuda.sh, with rights on Base Sepolia and ENS on the hackathon Ethereum Sepolia deployment. Built in the event window on a fresh repo.
howItsMade:
All four surfaces are Cloudflare Workers — api, member app, dashboard, gate scanner — on Hono, Drizzle over D1, R2, valibot, viem. EAS on Base Sepolia holds rights and delegations; D1 holds cards, member records, challenges, single-use consumption, entry logs and stamp credits. Any required chain read that fails, fails closed. Code: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/tree/main/apps → · Architecture: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/blob/main/docs/architecture.md →

Bearer and Signed verification. Standard Bearer rights use a counterfactual Coinbase Smart Wallet address computed by the factory with fuda's signer as its sole owner, so no member wallet setup or account deployment is needed to receive a pass; ownership transfer to the member is not implemented. Signed entry uses EIP-191 challenge-response through viem's verifyMessage, supporting ECDSA, ERC-1271 and ERC-6492.
+Private: passkey before issuance. WebAuthn PRF output derives viewing and spending keys and a stealth meta-address on-device (@noble/curves, WebCrypto). The issuer derives a fresh stealth address per right, attests the EAS right to it and publishes an ERC-5564 Announcement. The app fetches raw announcements from The Graph, matches locally, recovers the stealth signing key and signs an API challenge; the verdict shows in a modal on the member's device. Addresses differ per right, not per visit: issuer mappings and repeated presentations of the same UID are not hidden. packages/stealth-address.
Wallet passes built from scratch. Google save links are RS256 JWTs; the Apple .pkpass is signed with a detached CMS SignedData assembled with pkijs on WebCrypto. The hacky bit: signing a .pkpass normally means shelling out to OpenSSL, which a Worker can't do, so the whole manifest-hash-and-sign path is pure WebCrypto at the edge. packages/pass.
🏷️ ENS — one hybrid resolver, two kinds of name. One FudaResolver (ENSIP-10 wildcard) serves the whole tree: an active claimed venue's addr() is read from the ENSv2 User Registry on-chain, while member names are answered offchain by a signed CCIP-Read gateway in the api, and the resolver verifies that signature before answering. The venue claims its name with its own transaction, gated by an EIP-712 voucher fuda signs; gas is sponsored through fuda's ERC-7677 paymaster endpoint (Alchemy's verifying paymaster pays). viem's built-in Universal Resolver is overridden to the hackathon one. packages/ens-contracts, spec: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/blob/main/docs/specs/ens-naming.md →
📊 The Graph — composed Substreams. fuda_erc5564 extracts raw ERC-5564 Announcement events from the canonical singleton Announcer, parameterized by address, with zero fuda policy in it, so any ERC-5564 app can import the same .spkg without writing Rust. erc5564_eas_pipeline imports it by .spkg and composes it with an EAS Attested/Revoked module into one fuda_events stream, captured live from The Graph Market on Base Sepolia. The rights subgraph indexes EAS and the Announcer directly; the product's discovery path does not consume Substreams output. Spec: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/blob/main/docs/specs/substreams.md →
Raw and unfiltered on purpose. +Private discovery scans every announcement on-device; filtering per issuer or member inside the indexer would shrink the anonymity set. ADR: https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-graph-push-query-lanes.md →
Another hacky one. The subgraph's subgraph.yaml and schema-UID map are generated from the API's Sepolia configuration in wrangler.jsonc, and graph:prepare fails loudly while EAS_SCHEMAS or ANNOUNCER_FROM_BLOCK are unset, so the indexer and the Worker can't drift on which schema UIDs are live.

Built spec-first: docs/specs/ and docs/adr/ are in the repo and the code comments cite them by section. https://github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/tree/main/docs →

name: Aevum Protocol
description: Cryptographic proof your trading strategy ran honestly — live on Ethereum Mainnet.
projectDescription:
Aevum Protocol's Verifiable Backtest Oracle (VBO) solves the credibility problem in algorithmic trading. Anyone can show a great backtest there's no way to know if it was cherry-picked after the fact. VBO makes that impossible.
Traders commit a cryptographic hash of their strategy on-chain before the forward test window opens. Atlas Oracle cryptographically signs the BTC/USD price at both commit and attestation time using data from 905+ exchange sources. When the window closes, traders submit their logs and Aevum attests the results on-chain. The result is a permanent certificate proving the strategy ran honestly with zero look-ahead bias, independently verified benchmark prices, and no way to fake the timing.
Live on Ethereum Mainnet since September 3, 2026. First mainnet commitment active. 4 contracts deployed and verified on Etherscan.
howItsMade:
VBO v2 inherits Atlas Oracle's PullOracleConsumerStandard, making it the first trading strategy certification system with cryptographically signed benchmark prices. The architecture has 4 layers:
Smart contracts AgentIdentity, ReputationOracle v2, ReputationController v2, and VBO v2 deployed on Ethereum Mainnet. VBO v2 uses Atlas Oracle pull-mode price feeds (BTC/USD feed #626, 905+ exchange sources, ConsensusScore verified).
Serverless Atlas integration a Vercel serverless function fetches the Atlas signed price payload server-side and builds the VBO calldata before sending to MetaMask. This solves the Atlas payload requirement without exposing API keys in the browser.
Frontend React/Vite on Vercel with WalletConnect via Reown AppKit. Agent registration gate checks on-chain identity before allowing strategy commits. Certificate page displays Atlas-verified BTC/USD prices with ATLAS VERIFIED badge.
Infrastructure Supabase for commitment tracking, Resend for transactional emails, Stripe for payment processing, ImprovMX for email routing.
Two audits completed by Claude Opus 5 — 4 Critical, 6 High, 10 Medium, 8 Low findings all resolved. 36 Foundry tests passing. Hexens professional audit scoped, restarts at first investment close. Partner technology Atlas Oracle:
VBO v2 inherits PullOracleConsumerStandard from Atlas Oracle. This was the critical technical breakthrough without Atlas, BTC/USD benchmark prices on certificates would be self-reported. With Atlas, they are cryptographically signed by 905+ exchange sources and verified on-chain inside the smart contract. The atlasVerified flag on every Certificate struct proves both price points came from Atlas.

name: UNICA
description: Accept crypto, receive your asset. Uniswap converts, ENS names, The Graph indexes.
projectDescription:
UNICA is a testnet payment platform for ordinary businesses, live at https://unica.nfteria.click on Ethereum Sepolia. A business signs in with its wallet, and UNICA derives its identity, registers, payout wallet, and profile from on-chain ENS records. It can list one-off, recurring, or permanent products in an on-chain catalogue and share each product through a public shop, payment link, or QR code.
Before signing, a customer sees exactly what they will pay and what the business is guaranteed to receive. Same-asset USDC purchases settle directly. Plain ETH can be wrapped to WETH when required, while supported cross-asset register orders can use the UNICA market on Uniswap v4. Two payments are demonstrated on Sepolia: a 2 USDC purchase that settled directly, and a register order paid in WETH that converted to USDC through the UNICA market on Uniswap v4, verified on-chain and indexed.
A receipt says Paid only after UNICA's evidence rules verify the payment on-chain. Receipts identify the business and customer through forward-verified ENS names, include the transaction and explorer link, and report The Graph indexing only when the deployed subgraph returns that specific payment. Customers can view their purchases, while businesses can view payments and customers by verified ENS name.
The holder of unica.eth can set up a new business through the application. The app derives the required ENS record and lineage operations from current chain state and presents each transaction for separate wallet approval. The market infrastructure is deployed and source-verified across five test networks; the submitted identity, catalogue, shop, and demonstrated purchase run on Ethereum Sepolia. Testnet only, no real value, and unaudited.
howItsMade: Solidity 0.8.30 with Foundry: a market registry and factory, the UnicaMarketHook on Uniswap v4 (executor-only admission, the exact customer and amounts, a price band, an open unexpired sale), an executor, DirectSettlement for same-asset sales, ProductCatalog (one-off, recurring and permanent products with paidThrough, priced in ERC-20 assets whose deployed contracts expose readable metadata), TerminalAdmission (registers as ENS subnames with their own keys, revocable), and an ENSv2 resolver authority adapter read against the real Sepolia permissioned resolver. Vyper for the identity badge. Deployed stage by stage from the owner's own keystore after fork rehearsals, recorded into manifests, source-verified on Etherscan and Sourcify. The web app is static HTML and plain ES modules with no framework: an EIP-6963 wallet layer (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet), hand-written ABI encoding, the ENSv2 universal resolver for reverse lookups with a forward check before any name is shown, avatar text records per ENSIP-12, a name-derived gradient when a name has none. The join screen plans a new business as exact calldata (setAddr, setText, three registerLineage rows) from the chain's current state, skips rows that already stand, and asks the wallet to sign each in turn; the product form reads any ERC-20's symbol and decimals by address before it lists; when WETH is required, the checkout wraps ETH first, waits for confirmation, then performs any required approval before initiating the purchase. A small Node companion, also deployed as a Vercel function, keeps the node URL server-side behind a same-origin RPC pipe, reads logs through Etherscan V2 with Blockscout as the fallback, derives businesses from the authority's lineage and resolver records, and applies the evidence rules that decide Paid. A The Graph subgraph indexes the hook's receipts, direct settlements and catalogue sales; the receipt panel, the customer's purchases and the business's customers read it. 670 web test cases and 729 Foundry tests, plus guards for secrets and claims, run in CI on every push. Two details worth saying: the register reads the direct settler's own OrderCreated log back rather than trusting a return value, and the checkout explicitly serializes wrapping, approval, and purchase confirmation so a subsequent transaction cannot race an unmined prerequisite. A converted sale is priced by the register from the deployment's two Chainlink feeds, crossed in the app, and the sale line names each feed, its raw answer and its publish time.
